newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse prices pick up in modest trading.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse prices pick up in modest trading.

text.p: Bucharest share prices drifted higher at the bourse's second weekly session on Thursday, but volumes remained modest and turnover sagged to 33.2 million lei from the previous 55.5 million level.
"We expected mixed prices, but most of them picked up. In a way this was to be expected, as they had been falling for three sessions in a row," said one trader.
Six of 13 companies traded on the Bursa de Valori Bucuresti saw higher prices on Thursday. Three stocks fell and four had no trade.

"Today's turnover figure is laughable. It is the equivalent of a small company's wage fund," said another trader. "Buying interest is at a low. Investors seem determined to wait for fresh listings before committing more substantial amounts of money to the bourse."

The bourse said recently that 14 companies had applied for a listing and would join in trading and that it would handle public offers for another 14 state companies whose shares are then expected to trade on the exchange.
Azomures SA fertiliser maker clung to centre-stage on Thursday, taking 73 percent of total turnover. It closed 500 lei higher at 10,500.

The VAB-Index, an unofficial value-weighted index of all listed stocks computed by Vanguard SA securities, rose 2.4 percent from the previous session to 295.3 points after touching year lows for the previous three sessions. Its base was 1,000 points last November.
The other indepedent index, the BIG, compiled by Bucharest Investment Group, was not available.
